# R5 KDE supplier-variant test — 3 November 2026

**Preparation status: blocked; no R5 image pair has been produced.** The signed kernel build succeeded, but its boot RPM requires `uke-kernel-update >= 1.8.30`, `uke-kernel-update(device-local-video-import-v1) >= 1` and `uke-kernel-update(inactive-slot-no-image-backup-v1) >= 1`. R4 contains updater `1.8.24`. The offline RPM test refused the transaction before any package write; dependency checks were not bypassed. The instructions below describe the intended delivery and must be used only after a successful image workflow supplies the complete pair.

The smallest available signed dependency set is `uke-kernel-update`, `uke-installation-profile` and `uke-boot-integration`, all at `1.8.30-1.fc46.aarch64`. The updater requires the exact installation-profile revision, which requires the exact integration revision. Including them would be an explicit exception to preserving all R4 userland packages. KDE, Fedora libraries and the generic firmware would not need upgrades based on the observed dependency report; a complete nine-RPM transaction still needs validation if that exception is accepted.

| `uke-kernel-update-1.8.30-1.fc46.aarch64.rpm` | `af528aff8cccc1d7698b9d80682b51e6a0da148219e79a45343431dec64160ea` |
| `uke-installation-profile-1.8.30-1.fc46.aarch64.rpm` | `037b27a687c2d4c5c979c9fccbd7d12972bac65e992657e226172d714300ea81` |
| `uke-boot-integration-1.8.30-1.fc46.aarch64.rpm` | `7300cf7637af078af3d8fc126a392e67d7e097079792d243f19892e0defb4ada` |

This is an experimental **test-only pair**, distributed as a GitHub Actions artifact for 90 days. No GitHub Release is created. GitHub sign-in may be required. Download the complete `r5-kde-and-matching-boot-test` ZIP from the successful run of **Update R4 KDE to R5 test kernel (no Release)**. Keep a local copy before the artifact expires.

The existing verified R4 KDE EXT4 filesystem is updated offline with the six signed `7.3.1-1101.fc46.aarch64` kernel-family RPMs from [COPR build 11247906](https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/mcc45tr/uke-linux-test/build/11247906/). KDE, applications, languages, account setup, storage policy and generic OEM firmware retain their R4 versions. This is not a new root filesystem composition. The matching boot file comes byte-for-byte from that signed kernel's userdata boot bundle and replaces R4's shared boot. No GNOME image is supplied.

The candidate contains early selection for O82-36/O82-42 panels and Tianma/CSOT touch profiles. Host checks establish signed input and kernel/module/DT/boot consistency. **These exact R5 files have not been booted on a tablet.** Boot, display, touch, first-account setup, filesystem growth, swap and rollback require physical testing. A successful package build does not establish a fix for Issue #14.

## Files and verification

Extract the downloaded ZIP. In the directory containing both image files, run:

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

Continue only when both image checks pass. `PROVENANCE.json` records the R4 lineage, exact kernel source and automated check scope. The separate `r5-kde-update-receipts` artifact contains input hashes, the complete unchanged-userland comparison, RPM inventories and filesystem checks.

- `fedora-rawhide-kde-plasma-uke-senemos-system-031126-r5.img.zst`: compressed Android sparse EXT4 system image.
- `fedora-rawhide-uke-senemos-boot-031126-r5.img`: matching userdata boot, exactly **100,663,296 bytes**.

Use these two R5 files together. R4 roots and the R4 boot contain a different kernel ABI; mixing them with R5 is unsupported.

## Installation from a Linux PC

**Flashing userdata erases its existing Android or Linux system, applications, files and encryption metadata.** Back up needed data and keep your matching stock images and a working recovery route. Changing the active slot does not restore userdata.

Confirm an unlocked bootloader, the documented Xiaomi Pad 7 / POCO Pad X1 Uke variant, compatible stock slot-B firmware and the intended boot target. Preserve stock early firmware, calibration partitions and Android slot A. Do not make additional vbmeta or firmware changes for this test. See the [manual installation prerequisites](https://github.com/MCC45TR/uke-fedora-builder/blob/781079d9d3c2095005d3fe235f828d2a90553764/docs/PUBLIC-BUILD.md#output-and-manual-installation).

Decompress without deleting the downloaded archive:

```sh
zstd -d --keep fedora-rawhide-kde-plasma-uke-senemos-system-031126-r5.img.zst -o system.img
```

This produces an Android sparse image for fastboot. Do not flash the ZIP or `.zst` file. With the tablet in bootloader fastboot mode, inspect:

```sh
fastboot getvar product
fastboot getvar current-slot
fastboot getvar partition-size:userdata
fastboot getvar partition-size:boot_b
```

The product must be `uke`. Userdata must hold the **8,589,934,592-byte (8 GiB) expanded filesystem**; its capacity requirement is not the compressed or sparse file size. `boot_b` must hold at least **100,663,296 bytes** (`0x6000000`). Stop if the identity, capacities, firmware or recovery route are uncertain.

Once checks pass, run each command separately. Stop immediately if either flash fails; do not change the active slot or reboot into the incomplete pair:

```sh
fastboot flash userdata system.img
fastboot flash boot_b fedora-rawhide-uke-senemos-boot-031126-r5.img
fastboot set_active b
fastboot reboot
```

Do not run `fastboot -w` or format userdata afterwards. R4's existing original systemd-growfs and capacity gate remain responsible for first-boot growth before graphical setup. KDE uses Plasma Setup, contains no preset human account, and has SSH disabled. The image retains R4's unstable repositories; avoid a general package update before reporting the test result, to keep this kernel-only comparison meaningful.

## Test report and recovery

Record whether the device reaches graphical setup, the panel variant, display/touch operation and any failure stage. After successful setup, `uname -r` must show `7.3.1-1101`; also report filesystem capacity with `df -h /`. Do not claim complete hardware acceptance from one successful boot.

If boot fails, retain the first failure's slot state before further changes when possible:

```sh
fastboot getvar current-slot
fastboot getvar slot-successful:b
fastboot getvar slot-unbootable:b
fastboot getvar slot-retry-count:b
```

Report unsupported variables as such. A Mi logo/reboot sequence alone does not prove a kernel panic. Do not repeatedly reflash or alter vbmeta to obtain logs. Use the established matching stock recovery procedure to restore the device if needed; restoring userdata requires its own backup or reinstallation.
